# Type — mobile (React Native / Expo)

The React Native version of Type. Same Rust core as the desktop app
(`crates/type-core` via `crates/type-ffi`), same on-disk format, same git
sync — a folder of markdown files with front matter, `Feed`/`Archieve`
system folders, and per-folder `.type/settings.json`.

## The one interaction that matters

The app opens on a **blank page** — start typing immediately. **Swipe up**
and the page files itself into Feed while a fresh blank page slides in
underneath. Everything else (feed, folders, sync, recording, settings) is
secondary chrome reachable from the corner buttons.

## Running it

### Demo mode (no native build — works anywhere, including Expo Go)

```sh
npm install            # at the repo root (npm workspaces)
npm run start -w @typenotes/mobile
```

Without the generated native module the app boots against an in-memory mock
core (`@typenotes/mobile-core/mock-core`): fully interactive, nothing
persisted, banner at the bottom. UI work and the vitest suites never need a
native build.

### Real build (Mac)

1. Generate the native core module — see `packages/mobile-core/README.md`
   (ubrn codegen + iOS/Android Rust builds).
2. Wire it in `src/core/boot.ts` (uncomment the generated-module import).
3. Prebuild and run:

```sh
npm run prebuild -w @typenotes/mobile    # expo prebuild → ios/ + android/
npm run ios -w @typenotes/mobile         # or: npm run android -w @typenotes/mobile
```

The iOS app's Documents directory is user-visible in the Files app
(`UIFileSharingEnabled` + `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`), so working
folders created under it can be browsed, backed up, and pointed at from
other apps. True security-scoped external folders (iCloud Drive etc.) are a
later step.

## Layout

```
src/
  App.tsx                 boot + navigation container + demo banner
  navigation.ts           typed native-stack route table
  theme.ts                light/dark palette
  core/boot.ts            wires RawCore (generated native module or mock) + initCore
  lib/capture.ts          capture-page note lifecycle (pure, tested)
  lib/feed.ts             tree+previews → list rows (pure, tested)
  state/                  zustand stores: notes, settings (working folders), sync
  screens/                capture, feed, folder, editor, record, sync, settings
  ui/controls.tsx         small shared primitives for the utility screens
```

State flows one way: screens → `@typenotes/mobile-core/core-api` (typed
facade over the FFI) → Rust core. Stores cache the tree/previews/status and
re-fetch after mutations. Preview parsing, date labels, sync-error hints,
and frontmatter helpers come from `@typenotes/shared` — the same code the
desktop app uses.

## Transcription

Recordings are saved through the core (note + audio file + front matter,
`transcription_status: pending`), then queued according to the working
folder's `transcription_mode` (`.type/settings.json`, synced with the
notes): `assemblyai` queues cloud transcription from the phone, `desktop`
leaves recordings pending for a synced desktop's local Whisper, `native` is
the hook for an on-device recognizer via `queueProviderTranscriptions`
(provider registration not wired yet), `off` does nothing.

# Type — mobile (React Native / Expo)

The React Native version of Type. Same Rust core as the desktop app
(`crates/type-core` via `crates/type-ffi`), same on-disk format, same git
sync — a folder of markdown files with front matter, `Feed`/`Archieve`
system folders, and per-folder `.type/settings.json`.

## The one interaction that matters

The app opens on a **blank page** — start typing immediately. **Swipe up**
and the page files itself into Feed while a fresh blank page slides in
underneath. Everything else (feed, folders, sync, recording, settings) is
secondary chrome reachable from the corner buttons.

## Running it

### Demo mode (no native build — works anywhere, including Expo Go)

```sh
npm install            # at the repo root (npm workspaces)
npm run start -w @typenotes/mobile
```

Without the generated native module the app boots against an in-memory mock
core (`@typenotes/mobile-core/mock-core`): fully interactive, nothing
persisted, banner at the bottom. UI work and the vitest suites never need a
native build.

### Real build (Mac)

1. Generate the native core module — see `packages/mobile-core/README.md`
   (ubrn codegen + iOS/Android Rust builds).
2. Wire it in `src/core/boot.ts` (uncomment the generated-module import).
3. Prebuild and run:

```sh
npm run prebuild -w @typenotes/mobile    # expo prebuild → ios/ + android/
npm run ios -w @typenotes/mobile         # or: npm run android -w @typenotes/mobile
```

The iOS app's Documents directory is user-visible in the Files app
(`UIFileSharingEnabled` + `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`), so working
folders created under it can be browsed, backed up, and pointed at from
other apps. True security-scoped external folders (iCloud Drive etc.) are a
later step.

## Layout

```
src/
  App.tsx                 boot + navigation container + demo banner
  navigation.ts           typed native-stack route table
  theme.ts                light/dark palette
  core/boot.ts            wires RawCore (generated native module or mock) + initCore
  lib/capture.ts          capture-page note lifecycle (pure, tested)
  lib/feed.ts             tree+previews → list rows (pure, tested)
  state/                  zustand stores: notes, settings (working folders), sync
  screens/                capture, feed, folder, editor, record, sync, settings
  ui/controls.tsx         small shared primitives for the utility screens
```

State flows one way: screens → `@typenotes/mobile-core/core-api` (typed
facade over the FFI) → Rust core. Stores cache the tree/previews/status and
re-fetch after mutations. Preview parsing, date labels, sync-error hints,
and frontmatter helpers come from `@typenotes/shared` — the same code the
desktop app uses.

## Transcription

Recordings are saved through the core (note + audio file + front matter,
`transcription_status: pending`), then queued according to the working
folder's `transcription_mode` (`.type/settings.json`, synced with the
notes): `assemblyai` queues cloud transcription from the phone, `desktop`
leaves recordings pending for a synced desktop's local Whisper, `native` is
the hook for an on-device recognizer via `queueProviderTranscriptions`
(provider registration not wired yet), `off` does nothing.

content.text:
Done — all three changes are in, typecheck is clean (one pre-existing error unrelated to this, see below) and all test suites pass. Nothing is committed yet.

## Why the left swipe didn't work, and the new model

The menu was a full-width drawer driven by a JS gesture, and the capture page's full-screen text view was swallowing horizontal drags before the drawer's gesture could claim them. Instead of fighting that, I restructured navigation to match your mental model directly: **the menu is now the root of the native stack, and the capture page boots pushed on top of it** (`navigation.ts`, `App.tsx`). That means:

- **Home → swipe from left edge → menu.** This is now the *native* iOS back gesture (a system-level edge recognizer that wins over text views), so it's reliable. The hamburger does the same pop.
- **Menu → swipe leftward anywhere → fresh Home page** slides in from the right (plus the existing "New note" item).
- **Settings → sub-settings, Sync, folders, editor** are all pushed from the menu, so swiping from the left goes back one screen and eventually lands on the menu — exactly the behavior you described. This let me delete the old hacks (`gestureEnabled: false`, the "‹ Menu" back button, the drawer's reset-to-Capture effect). The drawer dependency is removed entirely; `drawer-content.tsx` became `screens/menu-screen.tsx`.

Yes, from a deep screen the swipe goes to the previous page, not Home — as you anticipated; that's inherent to this approach.

## Dictation button (Record screen removed)

The Record screen is gone. The mic is now a floating button in the bottom-right of the Home screen (`ui/dictation-button.tsx`):

- **Tap** → starts recording (button turns red with a stop icon and a live timer pill). **Tap again** → stops and saves.
- **Press and hold** → records only while held; releasing (after ~0.4s) stops and saves — your quick 5–10s clip case.
- Saving goes through the same core path as before (Feed note + audio + transcription queued per the folder's `transcription_mode`), with a brief "Saved — transcribing…" pill afterwards. It fades with the other icons while you type, but stays visible while recording so you can always stop it. If you leave the screen mid-recording it stops and saves rather than dropping the clip.

## Things to know when you test on device

- **A draft behind the menu now files into Feed.** Opening the menu pops the capture page, which flushes the draft (same as the swipe-up commit); coming back gives a blank page. Data is never lost, but text no longer "waits" behind the menu.
- **First-ever hold-to-record**: the mic permission prompt interrupts the hold, so that first recording behaves as tap-to-start — tap once more to stop. Subsequent holds work normally.
- **Rebuild needs `npm install`** on the Mac first (lockfile changed — drawer package removed), but no ubrn regen: nothing in `type-ffi` changed.
- Pre-existing, not from this change: `boot.ts` on this branch imports the generated native module uncommented, so `tsc` fails on any machine that hasn't run codegen (the file is gitignored). Worth deciding whether that should be re-commented for CI.
- On Android, the hardware back button on the menu now exits the app (the menu is the stack root) — fine for iOS-first, mentioning for completeness.

**1. UIKit:** нативный правый edge-жест существует как примитив — `UIScreenEdgePanGestureRecognizer` принимает `edges: .right`. Чего нет — это *встроенного системного* жеста навигации с правого края в LTR-локалях (поп-жест UINavigationController живёт на «ведущем» крае; забавно, что в RTL-локалях он как раз справа). Тут моя формулировка «не существует» была неверной — не существует только дефолтного поведения, сам жест полностью нативный.

**2. Практически важное (и тут я ошибся сильнее):** react-native-screens **уже вешает нативный recognizer на правый край** и активирует его в LTR, когда у верхнего экрана `stackAnimation == slide_from_left` и включён `customAnimationOnSwipe` — это прямо в коде `RNSScreenStack.mm`. Анимация `slide_from_left` на iOS реализована (`RNSScreenStackAnimator.mm`, `animateSlideFromLeftWithTransitionContext`) — комментарий в доках react-navigation «Android only» устарел. В react-navigation 7 эти опции называются `animation: 'slide_from_left'` + `animationMatchesGesture: true`.

**Что это меняет для твоей идеи:** она реализуется даже лучше, чем я говорил. Зеркальная схема:

- Menu остаётся корнем стека, но Capture пушится поверх него с `slide_from_left` + `animationMatchesGesture`.
- Тогда **свайп с правого края на Home = нативный pop**: домашняя уезжает влево, меню появляется справа — ровно твой жест, ноль JS.
- Гамбургер переезжает вправо-вверх (тот же `popTo`).
- На меню зеркалится кастомный жест: свайп вправо возвращает свежую домашнюю (въезжает слева).

То есть в твоём варианте открытие меню остаётся полностью нативным (мой главный аргумент «против» отпадает), кастомным остаётся только закрытие — как и сейчас, просто в зеркале. Единственное «против», которое остаётся — конвенция: в LTR правый край у юзеров ассоциируется с «вперёд» (Safari), а не с меню; но раз ты сам так ожидаешь — это не проблема.

# Type — mobile (React Native / Expo)

The React Native version of Type. Same Rust core as the desktop app
(`crates/type-core` via `crates/type-ffi`), same on-disk format, same git
sync — a folder of markdown files with front matter, `Feed`/`Archieve`
system folders, and per-folder `.type/settings.json`.

## The one interaction that matters

The app opens on a **blank page** — start typing immediately. **Swipe up**
and the page files itself into Feed while a fresh blank page slides in
underneath. **Swipe from the left edge** (or tap the hamburger) and the menu
slides in — feed and folders on top, sync and settings at the bottom; a
leftward swipe on the menu brings a fresh blank page back. The floating mic
button in the bottom-right dictates a voice note: tap to start and tap again
to stop, or hold it to record only while pressed.

## Running it

### Demo mode (no native build — works anywhere, including Expo Go)

```sh
npm install            # at the repo root (npm workspaces)
npm run start -w @typenotes/mobile
```

Without the generated native module the app boots against an in-memory mock
core (`@typenotes/mobile-core/mock-core`): fully interactive, nothing
persisted, banner at the bottom. UI work and the vitest suites never need a
native build.

### Real build (Mac)

1. Generate the native core module — see `packages/mobile-core/README.md`
   (ubrn codegen + iOS/Android Rust builds).
2. Wire it in `src/core/boot.ts` (uncomment the generated-module import).
3. Prebuild and run:

```sh
npm run prebuild -w @typenotes/mobile    # expo prebuild → ios/ + android/
npm run ios -w @typenotes/mobile         # or: npm run android -w @typenotes/mobile
```

The iOS app's Documents directory is user-visible in the Files app
(`UIFileSharingEnabled` + `LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace`), so working
folders created under it can be browsed, backed up, and pointed at from
other apps. True security-scoped external folders (iCloud Drive etc.) are a
later step.

## Layout

```
src/
  App.tsx                 boot + navigation container + demo banner
  navigation.ts           typed native-stack route table (menu is the root,
```
